meta.name: Detect pipeline stall risk with HubSpot, Slack, OpenRouter and Anthropic

parameters.content:
## Pipeline Risk & Stall Detector

### How it works
Flags deals stuck in your pipeline before they die quietly. A deterministic score (activity gaps, stage aging, single-threading, pushed close dates, missing next step) decides which deals are worth analyzing. High-risk deals go to a generator LLM for diagnosis, then a separate auditor LLM checks that diagnosis against the raw data before anything reaches Slack. Two independent triggers feed the same pipeline: a weekly HubSpot scan and a CRM-agnostic webhook, so it isn't locked to one CRM. Most templates in this space use either pure deterministic rules or a single unverified LLM pass, the dual-LLM audit and true dual-CRM coverage are the differentiators here.

### Setup
1. Attach a HubSpot credential (Private App token) to Fetch Open Deals (HubSpot).
2. Attach an OpenRouter credential to both OpenRouter Chat Model nodes (Generator + Auditor), a separate credential from HubSpot's.
3. Attach an Anthropic API credential to Anthropic Chat Model, this powers the Content Safety Guardrails checks and is a third, separate credential from HubSpot and OpenRouter.
4. Add a stage filter to Fetch Open Deals (HubSpot) once you know your pipeline's open-stage IDs.
5. Point Slack nodes at your workspace and update the #sales-alerts / #sales-ops-alerts channels.
6. Set crmBaseUrl on Write Alert Back to CRM, or swap it for a native CRM node.

nodes.name: Respond 202 Accepted
nodes.notes: Intentional fire-and-forget: alerting downstream is async, this ack just confirms receipt. If the CRM needs a synchronous verdict, expose a separate status-lookup endpoint instead of blocking here.

nodes.name: Fetch Open Deals (HubSpot)
nodes.notes: Native HubSpot node, resource=deal/getAll. Returns one n8n item per deal already, no Split Out step needed. Add a stage filter here (Filters field) once you know your pipeline's open-stage IDs -- these are account-specific in HubSpot, not standardized. hubspot_owner_id is an ID, not an email; Normalize Deal Data notes this gap for owner_email.

parameters.content:
## Triggers & Data Fetch
Weekly HubSpot scan or CRM-agnostic webhook, both feed Normalize Deal Data. Webhook responds 202 immediately since alerting is async.

## Deterministic Risk Scoring
Seven weighted factors produce a 0-1 score. Threshold 0.65 for high risk. Low/medium deals skip the LLM entirely.

## Dual-LLM Diagnosis
Generator writes the diagnosis, auditor checks it against raw data before it reaches Slack. Cost tracked per call. Errors route to #sales-ops-alerts.

## Guardrails & Duplicate Suppression
Schema check plus native PII/secrets scan (needs its own Anthropic credential) before alerting. Re-alerts only if score moves 0.10+ or 7+ days pass, via workflow static data.

## Alerting & CRM Write-back
Slack + CRM note fire in parallel. Falls back to #sales-alerts if owner_slack_id is missing.

nodes.name: Content Safety Guardrails
nodes.notes: Native n8n Guardrails node, scans the LLM-generated diagnosis text (not the JSON schema, that's the Code node before this) for PII and secret/key leakage before it reaches Slack or the CRM. NOTE: the exact parameter names (checks.pii, checks.secrets) and output shape are version-sensitive since this node is newer in the LangChain package -- verify the 'checks' options available in your instance's node panel and the field names read in Combine Guardrails Results below. If this node errors (e.g. misconfigured checks), it fails open rather than blocking the whole run: Combine Guardrails Results treats a content-safety error as skipped, not failed, so a broken optional check doesn't take down alerting. Remove or tighten that behavior if you'd rather fail closed.

nodes.name: Combine Guardrails Results
nodes.notes: Merges the schema check (Guardrails Check) with the content-safety check. Overall guardrails_passed requires both to pass; a skipped content-safety check (due to a node error) does not block on its own.

nodes.name: Anthropic Chat Model
nodes.notes: Language-model sub-node feeding Content Safety Guardrails via the ai_languageModel connection. Needs its own Anthropic API credential, separate from the HubSpot and OpenRouter credentials used elsewhere in this workflow. Powers whichever checks in Content Safety Guardrails require model reasoning (e.g. jailbreak/topical checks, if enabled) -- pattern-based checks like PII/secrets typically don't need it, but the node expects a language model connected regardless in this n8n version.
